question.problem:
$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-x(t)+y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-y(t)+1,\end{aligned}\,[\begin{aligned}x(0) \\ y(0)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] $$ Find the solution to the initial value problem above. *Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & t{e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].$*
$[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]=\,\,$ $1-{e}^{-t}-t{e}^{-t}$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]x(t)+g(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]$ and $g(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ So, the matrix of the system is $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].$

Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+g(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the solution of the initial value problem can be written as the sum of the homogeneous part and a particular solution:

$$
x(t)={{{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}\,x({t}_{0})}_{⏟}}_{\text{homogeneous part}}+{{{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s}_{⏟}}_{\text{particular solution}},
$$

where $x({t}_{0})$ is the initial condition vector. 

Let's evaluate each part separately:

- First, we find the homogeneous part. We are given that 

$$
{e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & t{e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].
$$

Since the initial conditions are given at $t={t}_{0}=0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})} & ={e}^{At}\,x(0) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & t{e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

- Next, we find the particular solution. Notice that 

$$
{e}^{A(t-s)}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-(t-s)} & (t-s){e}^{-(t-s)} \\ 0 & {e}^{-(t-s)}\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-(t-s)} & (t-s){e}^{-(t-s)} \\ 0 & {e}^{-(t-s)}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(t-s){e}^{s-t} \\ {e}^{s-t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}[\begin{aligned}(t-s){e}^{s-t} \\ {e}^{s-t}\end{aligned}]\text{d}s \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}(-s+t+1){e}^{s-t} \\ {e}^{s-t}\end{aligned}]}_{s=0}^{s=t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-(t+1){e}^{-t} \\ 1-{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1-(t+1){e}^{-t} \\ 1-{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-{e}^{-t}-t{e}^{-t} \\ 1-{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
